provenance.construction: Cyclic generalized-bicycle code over Z_305: H_X = [circ(a) | circ(b)], H_Z = [circ(b)^T | circ(a)^T], a = x^[22, 63, 79, 89, 97, 100, 110, 136, 141, 221, 234, 242, 265, 282, 283], b = x^[3, 40, 51, 53, 56, 67, 155, 169, 170, 173, 174, 191, 212, 239, 255, 281], both sparse multiples of a designed divisor g of x^305 - 1 (hex 0x14ab047041c41aa5) of degree 60, so k = 2 deg g = 120 by construction. Found by research/kit/search.py sample_cyclic_gb(6, seed=7), the designed-divisor sampler of PR #2790.
provenance.notes: Designed-divisor sampler (PR #2790, issue #2778): a and b are sparse multiples of a chosen degree-60 divisor g of x^305 - 1, so k = 2 deg g = 120 by construction. Distance: research/kit/surrogate.distance_rand_witness, fast backend, 10,000,000 trials per side, pair depth 32, seed 51, searched both sides and returned an X logical of weight 73 with nothing lighter on either side; the single-block annihilator attack (research/kit/annihilator.py, 200,000 trials, seed 11) found nothing lighter than 82. The Z witness is the image of the X witness under the transpose automorphism of the GB code (block swap composed with i -> -i mod 305), which maps H_X onto H_Z, so d_X = d_Z exactly. Earlier readings: 82 and 84 at 20,000 surrogate samples, 76 at 2,000,000 fast RIS trials. Witnessed upper bound, not certified.
